target.title: ci: reconcile pre-existing LOC ratchet drift
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Follow-up to #105894. Pull requests prepared before the LOC ratchet landed can still merge afterward and leave `main` with baseline drift. The original updater rejected every baseline increase, so it could not reconcile drift already present on the comparison base; unrelated work then failed the global check.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Compare baseline updates with each changed source file's actual LOC on the base tree. This permits catch-up only for drift already present on the base and still rejects same-PR growth, re-added files, and new oversized files.
- Ignore normal-check drift only when both the source path and its baseline entry are unchanged from the comparison base. Changed-file growth, shrink-without-baseline-lowering, baseline removal, and baseline-only tampering still fail.
- Parse Git path output with NUL delimiters so unusual valid filenames cannot evade changed-path matching.
- Refresh the snapshot to the current base after the pre-ratchet merge window exposed real drift.

## User Impact

None. Internal CI/tooling hardening only. The ratchet remains downward-only for every changed source file without blocking unrelated pull requests on drift inherited from `main`.

## Evidence

- Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01kxcqpxn1508vw9b4bvyx255c`: focused LOC suite passed 10/10; scripts typecheck, formatting, and live LOC check passed.
- Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01kxcqpxn1508vw9b4bvyx255c`: `pnpm check:changed` passed before the final base-aware filter; the filter then received focused proof above.
- Rebased onto current `main`; `node scripts/check-ts-max-loc.ts` passed without another snapshot refresh, proving inherited base drift no longer blocks the branch.
- Fresh autoreview: clean, no accepted/actionable findings.
- Exact-head GitHub CI remains the merge gate.

AI-assisted implementation and review. No agent transcript attached because transcript inclusion was not requested.
